rationale: On a petite frame, a kurta or kurti that ends around the thigh or knee leaves more of the leg line visible below the hem, which keeps the outfit in proportion with the height.
limitations: Long and floor-length kurtas are worn and loved at every height; this only gives a small lift to thigh and knee lengths, and the user's own style comes first.

rationale: Straight and tapered trousers and jeans follow the leg in one clean vertical line, which keeps the proportions balanced on a petite frame.
limitations: Wide-leg and flared cuts also work at any height, especially with a heel or a matching top; this is a gentle default and the user's silhouette preferences come first.

rationale: Small and medium print scales repeat several times across a petite frame, so the pattern reads as a whole rather than as one or two large motifs.
limitations: Bold, large prints are a style choice open to everyone; this only slightly favours smaller scales when the look includes a print.

rationale: On a tall frame, a kurta or kurti that reaches the knee, midi or ankle carries its length well and keeps the top and bottom of the outfit in proportion.
limitations: Shorter kurtis also suit tall wearers, particularly in casual looks; this only gives a small lift to longer lengths, and the user's own style comes first.

rationale: Wide-leg and flared trousers have room to fall fully on a tall frame, so the volume of the cut shows as designed from hip to hem.
limitations: Straight and tapered cuts are equally good choices for tall wearers; this is a gentle default and the user's silhouette preferences come first.

rationale: Medium and large print scales have space to show complete motifs across a tall frame, so the pattern keeps its intended design.
limitations: Small, fine prints suit tall wearers too; this only slightly favours larger scales when the look includes a print.
